title: Ways of Seeing · An illustrated journey into the uncanny
status: This is a separate exhibition; it does not change the city’s 3D scenes or visitor data.
scope: 212 artwork database records:80 locally illustrated CC0 works, the original100 research records,12 added modern viewing references and20 new M.C.Escher print references. All192 previous artwork objects and all80 local artwork images are preserved unchanged.

categories.title: Light as material
categories.question: When light becomes part of the work, what is the artwork made of?

categories.title: Colour in relationship
categories.question: How much of a colour belongs to its neighbours?

categories.title: Optical rhythm
categories.question: Can a still surface seem to move?

categories.title: Invented and constructed space
categories.question: How does an image persuade us that a space exists?

categories.title: Repetition and small rules
categories.question: How does one repeated decision become a complex whole?

categories.title: Motion and balance
categories.question: How can movement be present in a still or moving artwork?

categories.title: Material, surface and touch
categories.question: What can a material do that a picture alone cannot?

categories.title: Nature and changing atmosphere
categories.question: How does the same world become different through light and weather?

categories.title: Human presence and the act of looking
categories.question: Whose experience enters an artwork, and how?

categories.title: Dreams, faces & metamorphosis
categories.question: Where does a familiar thing become an impossible identity?

categories.title: Small signs, invented worlds
categories.question: How few marks does an imagined world need?

categories.title: The ordinary made uncanny
categories.question: What makes a place or object seem to be waiting for a story?

categories.title: Visions, myth & embodied ideas
categories.question: How can a picture give a thought or a vision a body?

categories.title: Magritte & surrealist connections
categories.question: What happens when recognisable things obey unfamiliar rules?

categories.title: M.C. Escher · impossible worlds & mathematical prints
categories.question: Which rule of a picture can remain convincing locally while failing across the whole?

categories.title: Artworks in the city
categories.question: How does an artwork change when you encounter it in a walkable city?

artist_pathways.title: Start here
artist_pathways.connection: Recognisable things, impossible relations. Ten studies, five preserved and five newly added, ask how a picture changes what we think an object, a title or a view can be.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Dream logic & hybrid identities
artist_pathways.connection: Try the human-headed marsh flower, then the inward world of Closed Eyes. The connection is imaginative ambiguity; Redon’s grainy visions differ from Magritte’s lucid object puzzles.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Unoccupied architecture
artist_pathways.connection: A ruin can carry an atmosphere without explaining a story. Compare this expectant landscape with the spatial unease of the modern surrealist references.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Signs becoming worlds
artist_pathways.connection: If Magritte makes the familiar strange, Klee lets simple marks invent their own logic. Follow a line until it becomes a person, a mechanism or a place.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Ordinary life & dark humour
artist_pathways.connection: Crowds, street furniture and an imagined future portrait make a familiar world unstable. This is a comparison of visual wit and unease, not a claim that their styles are identical.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Thoughts given bodies
artist_pathways.connection: A voice, a revelation and an abstract Truth become visible events. Compare the embodiment of ideas with Magritte’s games between words and pictures.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: The threshold of sleep
artist_pathways.connection: A sleeper and a mythic visitor allow incompatible worlds to share a picture. Ask whether a supernatural event belongs to the room, to a mind or to the image.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Story as an imagined world
artist_pathways.connection: An act of care sits within a spare, atmospheric landscape. Compare the unfolding of a symbolic story with Magritte’s refusal to give a puzzle one complete explanation.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Transformation through line & colour
artist_pathways.connection: Animals and their surroundings share visual rhythms. Metamorphosis can happen through a woodcut’s formal language as well as through impossible objects.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Uncanny interiors · disputed attribution
artist_pathways.connection: This reference is deliberately qualified: the museum discusses uncertainty between de Chirico and other surrealist attributions. Use it to consider how a convincing style can mislead an eye.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Collage & unlikely encounters
artist_pathways.connection: A believable fragment need not produce a believable whole. Compare the seam between found images with Magritte’s seamless-looking impossibilities.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Places as stages
artist_pathways.connection: Consider how architecture and stillness can make a place feel mentally reconstructed. Compare the atmosphere of a scene with the explicit puzzle of an object.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Forms before names
artist_pathways.connection: A landscape can feel spatially convincing even when its inhabitants evade identification. Compare this uncertainty with Magritte’s precisely named things.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Nocturnal signs
artist_pathways.connection: Try a language of signs and colour beside Magritte’s familiar objects. Both invite associations, but the visual vocabularies are very different.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Domestic expectations unsettled
artist_pathways.connection: An ordinary game title offers an entry to a less predictable world. Compare the expectations built by a title with those built by bodies and rooms.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Spaces in formation
artist_pathways.connection: An invented word opens onto a world whose forces seem to remain in motion. Compare this unstable spatial imagination with Magritte’s calmer visual surfaces.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Literature made visible
artist_pathways.connection: A companion, an ideal and an animal in disguise become pictures. Look at how a drawing moves between a character you can identify and a world you have to imagine.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: When creatures inherit our manners
artist_pathways.connection: Insects gather at a ball and objects gain suggestive identities. The comparison with Magritte is a question about categories: what happens when a thing behaves unlike the thing it is?
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: The unsettling logic of flight
artist_pathways.connection: Impossible flights can look like dreams, inventions or warnings. Compare an apparently understandable body with the uncertainty of its surrounding world.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Architecture that outgrows its map
artist_pathways.connection: A stair promises a route, but arches and platforms make orientation difficult. Compare a room you can describe with a building you cannot confidently navigate.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Precise lines, unresolved meanings
artist_pathways.connection: Geometric tools, monsters and dreams enter meticulously described spaces. Exact rendering can make an improbable scene persuasive without making its meaning certain.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: What the blank paper can do
artist_pathways.connection: A silhouette and a field of white carry worlds with very little modelling. Compare the power of omission with the clearly described objects in Magritte’s visual puzzles.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: A world reorganised by a viewpoint
artist_pathways.connection: Reflection, scale and repeated curves make familiar places surprising. These are comparisons in visual construction, rather than a claim that the landscape prints are surrealist works.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Pictures crossing into the world
artist_pathways.connection: Painted beings seem able to leave their images, while multi-panel scenes extend beyond a single sheet. Follow the boundaries between a picture, a story and an inhabited space.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Atmosphere and satirical disguise
artist_pathways.connection: A winter evening withholds information; an absurd costume makes authority visible in a different way. Notice how uncertainty and visual wit can arise from familiar materials.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: The spectator becomes the spectacle
artist_pathways.connection: An audience’s reactions and a musician’s interrupted attention turn ordinary looking and listening into theatrical subjects. Ask which side of a scene you occupy as a viewer.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Curatorial visual comparison, not a claim of documented influence.

artist_pathways.title: Prints that test space, surfaces & infinity
artist_pathways.connection: Escher (1898–1972) was a Dutch printmaker. Explore20 lithographs, woodcuts and wood engravings through impossible architecture, tessellation, reflection and topology. These records are official viewing references; their copyrighted images are not reproduced here.
artist_pathways.relationship_status: Dedicated artist study, with original looking prompts and verified print techniques.
